# MCP tools

<!-- Generated by tools/mcp_tool_reference.py from manifests/mcp_tools.json; do not edit. -->

The tools every GUI.Forms program serves under `--mcp-shared` and `--mcp-fcfs` ([hosts and capabilities](hosts-and-capabilities.md): reads need no control; an act takes control first), as a built program lists them. A program adds its own beside them with `register_model_tool` (names with underscores, such as `<program>_<tool>`), and its commands are tools named `command_<id>`; neither is listed here. Every tool refuses an argument its schema does not name.

## `windows`

**Windows.** Every window: stable ID, title, active, modal, size.

No arguments.

## `snapshot`

**Snapshot.** The control tree as an outline: role, name, [stable ID], states, value, the actions each node takes and what its press opens (needs_user: it opens a dialog the user answers; instead= names a tool that does the same without one; default and cancel: the buttons Enter and Escape press). A virtualised list says how many rows it does not show. Narrow it with root and filter; actions false leaves the actions out. A read: needs no control.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `root` | string | no |  |
| `filter` | string | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |
| `bounds` | boolean | no |  |
| `actions` | boolean | no |  |

## `find`

**Find.** Nodes by role, name (any case, part of it) and state, each with its [stable ID] and parent; cheaper than a snapshot when you know what you look for.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `role` | string | no |  |
| `name` | string | no |  |
| `state` | string | no |  |
| `within` | string | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |

## `act`

**Act.** A semantic action on a node (press, select, expand, collapse, focus, set_value, increment, decrement, show_menu, close), scroll_into_view, or invoke_command on a command's stable ID. A row a virtualised list does not show is reached by its ID. A dialog you opened may be closed (close on the dialog, as Cancel), never submitted. close on a program window's own ID closes the window: save first, then close. A question the program raises during an act (save changes?) is yours and never shown: with no on_unsaved the act stops there, the program stays as it was, and the reply gives the question and its choices; on_unsaved save or discard answers it. Waits for idle and replies with what changed; terse gives counts. Acts need control: in a shared launch (--mcp-shared) your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows).

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `target` | string | no | a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID |
| `within` | string | no | an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats |
| `action` | one of `press`, `select`, `expand`, `collapse`, `focus`, `set_value`, `increment`, `decrement`, `show_menu`, `close`, `scroll_into_view`, `invoke_command` | no |  |
| `value` | string | no |  |
| `terse` | boolean | no |  |
| `on_unsaved` | one of `save`, `discard` | no | The answer to a save changes? question the act raises: save or discard; without it the act stops at the question and replies with it. |

## `reset`

**Reset.** Puts the interface back in order: closes the dialogs you opened (as Cancel), popups and menus, tooltips and drags, releases pointer capture, and stops content that froze; replies with what it reset and what it left (a dialog the user opened). Acts need control: in a shared launch (--mcp-shared) your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows).

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |

## `pointer`

**Pointer.** Pointer input through the program's own input path: move, hover, click, double_click, right_click, down, up, drag, wheel. Aim with a target (offset inside it, default its centre) or with position in window coordinates, not both. A drag presses at that point and moves through path: with a target, path points are in the target's space like offset; without one, window coordinates like position. Acts need control: in a shared launch (--mcp-shared) your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows).

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `target` | string | no | a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID |
| `within` | string | no | an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats |
| `action` | one of `move`, `hover`, `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `down`, `up`, `drag`, `wheel` | no |  |
| `offset` | object | no | Logical pixels from the target's top-left corner (its bounds as snapshot bounds gives them) |
| `position` | object | no | Window coordinates: logical pixels from the top-left corner of the window's content area, the space of snapshot bounds |
| `path` | array of object or array of number | no |  |
| `button` | one of `primary`, `secondary`, `middle` | no |  |
| `modifiers` | array of string | no |  |
| `delta` | object | no | Wheel notches: y -1 scrolls down one notch, y 1 up; x scrolls sideways. Default {x: 0, y: -1} |
| `terse` | boolean | no |  |

## `keyboard`

**Keyboard.** Key chords ("Ctrl+S") and sequences, committed text, and composition, to the focused control or to a target focused first. Acts need control: in a shared launch (--mcp-shared) your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows). Replies with what changed, as act does.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `target` | string | no | a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID |
| `within` | string | no | an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats |
| `keys` | string or array of string | no |  |
| `text` | string | no |  |
| `composition` | object | no |  |
| `terse` | boolean | no |  |

## `text`

**Text.** A node's whole text: a text control's value, selection and lines (with select, sets the selection, UTF-8 byte offsets); any other node's full name, value and description, such as a label cut in the outline.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `target` | string | no | a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID |
| `within` | string | no | an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats |
| `select` | object | no |  |

## `wait`

**Wait.** Waits until the next frame, idle, a time (ms), a condition on a node (state, value, exists) or a user step done.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `target` | string | no | a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID |
| `within` | string | no | an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats |
| `until` | one of `frame`, `idle`, `ms`, `node`, `user_step` | no |  |
| `ms` | number | no |  |
| `timeout_ms` | number | no |  |
| `state` | string | no |  |
| `value` | string | no |  |
| `exists` | boolean | no |  |
| `step` | string | no |  |

## `capture`

**Capture.** A window or control as a PNG, drawn fresh from the current state; a window's open popup windows (menus, drop-downs) and its tooltip window are composited over it unless popups is false. Password fields are painted out. The in-use sign (the band, AI mode's stripes) is left out unless include_sign is true, so you see the program as its user does without a model. points [{x, y}, ...] (or [x, y] pairs; logical units from the captured area's top left, at most 1024) answers the colour at each instead of an image, to check a drawing cheaply. path saves the PNG to a file and replies with its path, size and dimensions (the command folder, given no path, saves to capture-<n>.png in its own folder). A read: needs no control.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `target` | string | no | a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID |
| `within` | string | no | an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats |
| `mode` | one of `rendered` | no |  |
| `points` | array of object or array of number | no |  |
| `scale` | number | no |  |
| `margin` | number | no |  |
| `include_overlays` | boolean | no |  |
| `popups` | boolean | no |  |
| `include_sign` | boolean | no |  |
| `path` | string | no | Save the PNG to this file (an absolute path ending .png) and reply with its path, size and dimensions instead of the image |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | Replace a file already at path |

## `inspect`

**Inspect.** Beyond accessibility, sections chosen with what: state, layout, paint, metrics, dispatcher, interaction, session, schema, clipboard, summary, layout_reasons, resources, events. With a target, state, layout and schema by default; without, metrics, dispatcher and interaction.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `target` | string | no | a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID |
| `within` | string | no | an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats |
| `what` | array of one of `state`, `layout`, `paint`, `metrics`, `dispatcher`, `interaction`, `session`, `schema`, `clipboard`, `summary`, `layout_reasons`, `resources`, `events` | no |  |

## `batch`

**Batch.** Several steps in one call with one combined reply: each step is {"tool": name, ...that tool's arguments} or an expect guard {"expect": "node"|"visual", target, state, value, exists, drawn}; the batch stops at the first failure or unmet expectation; at most 512 steps. terse gives each act's changes as counts.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | array of object | yes |  |
| `stop_on_error` | boolean | no |  |
| `terse` | boolean | no |  |

## `release_control`

**Release control.** Gives the program back to the user and ends AI mode. In a --mcp-shared launch your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows when it ends) and you then hold control until you release it or 30 s pass without a call; in a --mcp-fcfs launch your first act takes control at once and you keep it until you release it or the user takes it back. Reads never need control.

No arguments.

## `close`

**Close.** Quits the program: every program window is asked to close, as the user's quit does. An act: it takes control first as any act does in this launch (at once under --mcp-fcfs; under --mcp-shared the user may refuse). A question the program raises (save changes?) is yours and never shown: with no on_unsaved nothing closes and the reply names it; on_unsaved save or discard answers it. Unlike disconnect, which ends your session (and, with mode hard, closes), close is about the program.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | string | no | a window's stable ID or title; default the active window |
| `on_unsaved` | one of `save`, `discard` | no | The answer to a save changes? question the act raises: save or discard; without it the act stops at the question and replies with it. |

## `disconnect`

**Disconnect.** Ends your session and closes the program cleanly. An act: it takes control first as any act does in this launch (under --mcp-shared the user may refuse, and the program stays open). The usual path: save your work with the program's save tool, then disconnect. mode soft (the default) never closes over unsaved work and never shows anything: if the program asks to save, nothing closes, and the reply names what to save; save it, then disconnect again. mode hard ends the session regardless: control returns to the user and the program's own save question is shown to the user, or, with discard_unsaved true, unsaved changes are discarded and nothing is asked.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | one of `soft`, `hard` | no |  |
| `discard_unsaved` | boolean | no |  |
